The 'previous task' (vorige Aufgabe) asks when a binary form f of degree n can be written as Σ c_i·ℓ_i^n, where the ℓ_i are the linear factors of a second binary form φ. Classically, this is possible exactly when φ is apolar to f, meaning the relevant (last) transvectant or apolarity pairing vanishes. This is Sylvester's apolarity theory, which today is the apolarity lemma for Waring decompositions of binary forms. The note only says 'closure problem for the previous task'. evidence.claim: Sylvester showed that a generic binary cubic can be written as a sum of two cubes of linear forms. This is a case of representing a form as a sum of powers of linear forms, which is the setting of the 'previous task'.
Writing binary forms as sums of powers of linear forms goes back to Sylvester and Gundelfinger, and the apolarity approach to the Waring problem started with their work.
In the modern form of Sylvester's theorem, decompositions of a binary form are described using the apolarity lemma (Iarrobino–Kanev, Lemma 1.15).
